git add internal/audit/scan_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(test): make the write-failure rollback tests write real bytes (PR #509 review, J1)

The writeFile stub in TestAppendMonotonic_WriteFailureTruncatesBack,
TestAppendMonotonic_WriteFailureThenSuccessAppendsExactlyOnce, and
TestAppendMonotonic_WriteFailureRollbackFsyncAlsoFailsIsReported returned
(0, err) without writing anything, so the live file was empty before AND
after the call regardless of whether rollbackTruncate ever ran -- the
fifth instance on this branch of a test guarding its own fixture rather
than the property it claims to pin, and this one guarded the fix landed
one commit ago. shortRealWriteThenError now writes a real half-length
prefix before failing, so only the truncate can bring the file back to
empty. TruncatesBack was already non-vacuous once bytes hit disk; the
ThenSuccess test needed an added intermediate empty-file assertion too,
because AppendMonotonic's unrelated torn-tail auto-heal on the retry's
reopen would otherwise still converge to "exactly 1 line" even with
rollbackTruncate deleted, masking the same defect a second way.

Falsified: deleted rollbackTruncate from the write-failure branch,
confirmed all four write-failure tests fail (including the pre-existing
short-write test, which was already non-vacuous); restored the branch
verbatim (git diff empty) and confirmed all pass. Also checked the
sync-failure siblings per the reviewer's request -- they stub only
fsyncFile and let the real Write run, so the full line is genuinely on
disk before the rollback; falsifying the sync-failure branch the same
way confirmed all three sync-failure tests are already non-vacuous.

make check green (race detector, all packages).
EOF
)"
